2. Definitions.‑‑‑
In this Ordinance unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context‑‑
(a)
"Academic Council" means the Academic Council of the Institute;"
(b)
"Authority" means any of the Authorities of the Institute specified
in this Ordinance;
(c)
"Board" means the Board of Governors of the Institute;
(d)
"Chairman" means the Chairman of the Board;
(e)
"Dean" means the Chairman of the Board of Faculty;
(f)
"Director" means administrative head of a campus;
(g)
"Government" means the Government of Sindh;
(h)
"Institute" means the Preston Institute of Management, Science and
Technology;
(i)
"Patron" means the Patron of the Institute;
(j)
"Prescribed" means prescribed by rules or regulations;
(k)
"Professor Emeritus" means a retired Professor working in the
Institute in honorary capacity;
(l)
"Rector" means the Rector of the Institute "
(m)
"Regulations" means regulations made under this Ordinance,
(n)
"Rules" means rules made under this Ordinance.
(o)
"Society" means "the Management Educational Society"
registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.

3. Establishment of the
Institute.‑‑‑ (1) There shall be established an Institute
to be known as a Preston Institute of Management, Science and Technology at
Karachi consisting of the Patron, the Chairman, the Rector, the Deans, the
Chairmen of the Teaching Departments, the members of the Board, the members of
the Academic Council and such other officers as may be prescribed.
(2) The
Institute shall be a body corporate by the name of the Preston Institute of
Management, Science and Technology, owned, managed and administered by the
Society having perpetual succession and a common seal and shall sue and be sued
by the said name.
(3) The
Institute shall be open to all persons of either sex and whatever religion,
race, class, caste, creed, colour or domicile who are academically qualified
for admission to the courses of study offered by the Institute and no such
person shall be denied the privileges of the Institute on the ground only of
sex, religion, creed; race, caste, class, colour or domicile.
(4) The moral
and ethical codes applied to the Institute and its constituent institutions
will be based on and derived from the cardinal principles and the guidance
embodied in the Holy Qur'an and the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him).

4. Powers and functions of the
Institute.‑‑‑ Subject to the instructions prescribed by
Government or the University Grants Commission, the Institute shall have the
powers‑‑
(i) to provide
for instruction and training in management, computer sciences and technology,
and other allied disciplines in such manner as it considers appropriate;
(ii) to admit
and hold examinations and to award and confer degrees, diplomas, certificates
and other academic distinctions on and to the persons who have been admitted to
and have passed its examinations under the prescribed conditions;
(iii) to confer
honorary decrees or other distinctions on approved persons in the prescribed
manner; .
(iv) to
establish facilities, teaching departments,, research institutes and other
learning centres in the ordained branches of leaning and to provide and support
other facilities for education, professional training and research;
(v) to acquire
and hold property, both movable and immovable, to lease, sell or otherwise
transfer and movable or immovable property vesting in it;
(vi) to
cooperate with other institutes and universities public authorities in such
manner and for such purposes as may be prescribed;
(vii) to institute Professorship,; Associate
Professorship, Assistant Professorship and Lecturer-ship; '
(viii) to create
posts for research, administration and other related purposes;
(ix) to
institute and award fellowships, scholarships, exhibitions, bursaries, medals
and prizes under the prescribed conditions;
(x) to supervise
and control the discipline of the students of the Institute, and to promote the
extra-curricular and recreational activities of such students, and to make
arrangement for promoting their health and general welfare;
(xi) to demand
and receive such fees and other charges as it may determine; provided that ten
percent seats will be reserved for meritorious, poor candidates on free ship or
scholarship basis;
(xii) to enter
into, carry out, vary or cancel contracts;
(xiii) to
receive and manage properties, grants, bequests, trusts, gifts, donations,
endowments and other contributions made to the Institute and obtain loans or
aids and to invest any funds representing such property, grants, bequests,
trusts, gifts, donations, endowments or contributions in such manner as it may
deem fit;
(xiv) to
undertake such research as it may determine in the ordained branches of
learning;
(xv) to provide
for the printing and publication of research and other
(xvi) to appoint
members of various bodies and committees, as the Board may determine, for
academic and administrative activities;
(xvii) to
prescribe terms and conditions, and powers and duties of officers including
teachers and staff;
(xviii) to
establish academic linkages and collaborative activities with other
institutions for the betterment of academic standards; and
(xix) to do all
such ‑ other acts and things as may be required to further its objectives
and perform its functions.

7. Visitation.‑‑‑.
(1) The Patron may cause an inspection or inquiry to be made in respect of any
matter connected with the affairs of the Institute and shall, from time to
time, direct any person or persons to inquire into or carry out inspection of‑‑
(i) the
Institute, its buildings, libraries, and other facilities;
(ii) any
institution or department maintained by the Institute;
(iii) the
adequacy of financial and human resources;'
(iv) the
teaching, research, curriculum, examination and other matters of the Institute;
and
(v) such other
matters as may be specified by him.
(2) The Patron
shall communicate to the Board his views with regard to the results of the
visitation and shall, after ascertaining the views of the Board, advise the
Board, on the action to be taken by it.
(3) The Board
shall, within such time as may be specified by the Patron, communicate to him
such action, .if any, as has been taken or may be proposed to be taken upon the
results of visitation. ,
(4) Where the
Board does not, within the time specified, take action to the satisfaction of
the Patron, the Patron may issue such directions as he deems fit and the Board
shall comply with all such directions.
(5) The Patron
shall have full powers to take any action as he may deem fit against the
institution, including its closure, if found indulging in any. subversive or
unlawful activity.

10. Powers and duties of the
Rector.‑‑‑ (1) The Rector shall be the chief academic and
administrative officer of the Institute and shall be responsible for the
implementation of the decisions of the Board and the execution‑ of the
programmes of the Institute in accordance with the guidelines and policies
formulated by the Board.
(2) The Rector
shall‑‑
(i) submit plans
of work and budget estimates of the Institute for the consideration of the
Board;
(ii) direct the
activities connected with the execution of programmes of instruction, training,
research, or services to the community;
'(iii) authorize
expenditure provided for in the approved budget and to appropriate funds
within' the same major head of the expenditure and report it to the Board in
the next meeting; a
(iv) sanction
and re appropriate an amount as fixed and revised by the Board from time to
time for an unforeseen item not provided for in‑ the budget and report to
the Board in the next meeting;
(v) submit
reports on the activities of the Institute and the execution of the plans of
work to the Board in accordance with the rules;
(vi) create and fill temporary posts for a
period not exceeding six months; and
(vii) undertake
any work assigned by the Board.

(iii) Secretary

17. Powers and Functions of
the Board.‑‑‑ The Board shall exercise and perform the
powers and functions as follows:‑‑
(i) to hold,
control of and administer the properties, funds, assets and resources of the
Institute;
(ii) to govern
and regulate, with the advice of the Finance and Planning Committees, the
finances, accounts and investments of the Institute and for that purpose,
appoint such agents as it may deems fit;
(iii) to
consider annual and revised budget estimates. and to re appropriate funds from
one major head of expenditure to another;
(iv) to transfer
and accept transfer of movable or immovable property on behalf of the
Institute;
(v) to enter
into, vary, carry out and cancel contracts on behalf of the Institute;
(vi) to cause
proper books of accounts to be kept for all sums of money received and expended
by the Institute and for the assets and liabilities of the Institute;
(vii) to receive
and manage any property transferred and grants, bequests, donations, endowments
and other contributions made to the Institute;
(ix) to accord
approval to provide the buildings, libraries, premises, furnitures, apparatus,
equipments and. other means required for carrying out the work of the
Institute;
(x) to institute
professorship, associate professorship, assistant professorship, lecturer ship
and other teaching and create administrative post or to suspend or abolish such
posts;
(xi) to make
appointments on the recommendation of the Selection Board to the posts of
teachers, officers and such other cadres as may be determined by the Board;
(xii) to appoint
Emeritus Professors on such terms and conditions as
(xiii) to confer
Honorary Degrees with the approval of Patron in the fields of ordained
disciplines in accordance with the conditions prescribed;
(xiv) to
prescribe ‑the duties of officers, teachers, and other employees of the
Institute;
(xv) to suspend,
impose penalty and remove from service officers (other than the Rector)
teachers and other employees in the manner prescribed;
(xvi) to‑
appoint members to the various authorities in accordance with the provisions of

(xvii) to frame

to the Chairman for approval;
(xviii) to
consider and approve the draft rules submitted to it; and
(xix) to
delegate any of its powers. to an authority or officer or a committee or
sub-committee.

18. Meeting of the Board.‑‑‑
(1) The Board shall, meet at least twice in a year on the dates fixed by the
Rector in consultation with the Chairman, provided that a special meeting may
be called at any time on the direction of the Chairman or on a requisition made
by not less than four members of the Board to consider a matter of urgent
nature.
(2) Not less
than ten clear days' notice of a special meeting‑shall be given to the
members of the Board and the agenda of the meeting shall be restricted to the
matter for which the special meeting is called.
(3) The quorum
for a meeting of the Board shall be one‑half of its members, a fraction
being counted as one.
(4) The
decisions of the Board shall be expressed in terms of the views of the majority
of the members present and voting and in case of tie, the Chairman shall
exercise a casting vote.

19. Academic Council.‑‑‑
(1) The Academic Council shall consist of‑‑‑
(i) The Rector
who shall be the Chairman,
(ii) The Deans;
(iii) The
Directors;
(iv) The
Institute Professors including Emeritus and distinguished Professors;
(v) Nominee of
the Education Secretary Government of Sindh not below the rank of Deputy Secretary;
(vi) Advisor
(Academics) of the University Grants Commission or his‑nominee;
(vii) the
Chairmen of the Teaching Departments;
(viii) three
eminent persons known for their intellectual calibre on international level,
service to. society or leadership in profession nominated by the Chairman on
the recommendation of the Rector;'
(ix) the
Controller of Examinations;
(x) the
Librarian; and
(xi) the
Registrar who shall act as its Secretary.
(2) Members
appointed by nomination shall hold office for three years and shall be eligible
for re‑nomination: .
(3) The quorum
for a meeting of the Academic Council shall be one ‑third of the total
number of members, a fraction being counted as one.

20. Powers and Duties of the
Academic Council.‑‑ (1) The Academic Council shall be the
highest academic body of the Institute, and shall, subject to the provisions of
this Ordinance and the regulations, have the powers to lay down proper,
standards of instruction, scholarship,, research and examinations and to
regulate and promote the academic life of the Institute. .
(2) In
particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing
provisions,, the Academic Council shall have the powers‑‑
(i) to advise
the Board on academic matters;
(ii) to regulate
the admission of students to the courses of studies and holding of
examinations;
(iii) to propose
to the Board, schemes for the constitution and organization of faculties
teaching departments, campuses and Board of Studies;
(iv) to consider
or formulate proposals for the planning and development of teaching and
research in the Institute;
(v) to make
rules on the recommendations of the Board of Faculties or the Boards of Studies
prescribing the course of studies and the syllabi;
Provided that,
if the recommendations of the Board of Faculties and Boards of Studies are not
received by the prescribed date, the Council may, subject to the approval of
the Board, continue for the next year, the courses of studies already
prescribed for an examination;
(vi) to
recognize the examinations of other institutes, universities or examining
bodies as equivalent to the corresponding examinations of the institute;
(vii) to propose
rules for submission to the Board; and
(viii) to
perform such other functions as may be prescribed:

21. Regulations.‑‑‑
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Ordinance, the Board may make regulations
which may prescribe all or any of the following matters namely‑‑‑
(a) terms and
conditions of service of employees of the Institute, including scales of pay,
constitution of pension,, insurance, gratuity, provident fund, benevolent fund
and other fringe benefits;
(b) terms and
conditions of contractual appointment of teachers, researchers and officers;
(c) constitution
and functions of the. Selection Board for selection of candidates for
appointment to various posts of teachers and other officers and staff;
(d)
establishment of faculties, teaching departments and other academic units and
divisions and their management;
(e) powers and
duties of officers and teachers;
(f) conditions
under which the Institute may enter into arrangements, partnership,
collaboration with other public, , Government or private organizations for
purpose of instruction, research and other scholarly activities for the
betterment of the Institute;
(g) condition of
appointment of Professor Emeritus , and distinguished Professors;
(h) award of
honorary degrees;
(i) standards
for evaluation of efficiency and exercising disciplinary measures over the
employees of the Institute;.
(j) acquisition
and administration of properties and investment of the Institute; and
(k) all other
matters which under this Ordinance are required to be or may be prescribed by
the regulations.
(2) The draft of
the regulations shall be proposed by the Board for approval by the Chairman who
may refer them back to the Board for
(3) The Chairman
shall have the powers to assent to the regulations submitted to him for
approval.
(4) No
regulation shall be valid until assented to and signed by the Chairman.

The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby published for

23. The Institute fund, audit
and accounts.‑‑‑ (1) The Institute shall have a fund to
which shall be credited income from fees, donations, trusts, bequests,
endowments, grants, contributions and any other sources.
(2) No
contribution or grant which may directly or indirectly involve any immediate or
subsequent financial liability of the Institute or which may involve an
activity not included in its programmes for the time being shall be accepted
without the prior approval of the Board.
(3) The accounts
of the Institute shall be maintained in such form and in such manner as may be
prescribed by the rules.
(4) The accounts
of the Institute shall be audited each year within four months of the closing
of the financial year of the Institute by Chartered Accountant appointed by the
Board.
(5) The
accounts, together with the report of the auditor thereon, shall be submitted
to the Board for approval.
(6) The
auditor's report shall certify that the auditor has complied with the standards
of audit and certification laid down by the Institute of Chartered Accountants
of Pakistan. ,

25. Bar of jurisdiction.‑‑‑
No Court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any proceedings, grant any
injunction or make any order in relation to anything done in good faith or
purported to have been done or intended to be done under this Ordinance.

27. Removal of difficulties.‑‑‑
(1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to any of the provisions of this
Ordinance, the Chairman may make such orders, which are consistent with the
provisions of this Ordinance.
(2) Where this
Ordinance makes any provision foe anything to be done., but no provision or
insufficient provision has been made as respecting the authority by whom, or
the time at which, or the manner in which it shall be done then it shall be
done by such authority, or at such time, or in such manner, as the Chairman may
direct.
